spec_family.name: Exterior Stucco & EIFS Wall Coating
spec_family.description: Combined prime and finish coat painting for exterior stucco and EIFS (Exterior Insulation and Finish System) wall surfaces. Covers full prep (crack assessment with >1/8 inch structural hard stop, EIFS knock test for delamination, cure verification on traditional stucco, moisture testing, pressure wash branched by substrate type, mildew/efflorescence treatment, surface patching with texture match, caulking stucco-to-trim joints), substrate-specific primer (alkali-resistant on traditional stucco pH 12-14, standard acrylic on EIFS), and finish coats (acrylic or elastomeric coating system). HARD CONSTRAINT: EIFS = acrylic coating ONLY — elastomeric is PROHIBITED on EIFS (catastrophic moisture entrapment). Spray_backroll is the primary application method — spray-only is PROHIBITED on textured stucco (backroll forces coating into texture recesses for continuous DFT). Texture profile (smooth/sand/lace/dash) is the dominant cost driver via DUAL multiplier on both labor rate (SF/hr) and material consumption (SF/gal). Uses SF as primary UOM. Single paintable item: ITM_STUCCO_WALL. 6 configuration dimensions: quality_tier, substrate_type, texture_profile, coating_system, application_method, sheen. Window/door protection is NOT this spec's responsibility — belongs in window/door specs.

includes: Crack assessment (FIRST prep task — >1/8 inch = HARD STOP for structural evaluation)
EIFS knock test for delamination detection (EIFS only — delamination = HARD STOP)
Cure verification (traditional stucco — 30-day standard, 7-day with alkali-resistant primer)
Moisture testing (traditional stucco — MC <12% hard stop per ASTM D4263)
EIFS insurance verification (CGL policy covers EIFS work or EIFS-specific rider obtained)
Pressure wash — substrate-specific (1,500-3,000 PSI traditional stucco; <500 PSI EIFS)
Mildew eradication (bleach solution 1:3, scrub, rinse — both substrate types)
Efflorescence treatment (traditional stucco only — water/TSP/acid cleaning hierarchy)
Cosmetic crack patching (<1/8 inch with elastomeric caulk)
Surface defect patching with texture match
Full field primer coat — alkali-resistant on traditional stucco (mandatory pH 12-14), acrylic on EIFS
Finish coat application — acrylic (1-2 coats by QT) or elastomeric (2 coats mandatory, traditional stucco only, QT3+ only)
Interstage inspection, light sand at QT4 on anomalies only, dust removal
Landscape perimeter protection (LF-based along house perimeter)
Fixture and utility masking (light fixtures, HVAC units)

configuration_dimensions.description: Quality tier controlling coat count, inspection scrutiny, interstage sanding, cleaning intensity, and defect tolerance.
configuration_dimensions.notes: QT2=economy (single acrylic finish coat, light wash, acrylic only — elastomeric NOT available at QT2). QT3=standard (2 finish coats, full wash, acrylic or elastomeric). QT4=premium (2 finish coats, TSP wash, interstage sand on anomalies, premium materials, raking light inspection). QT5 excluded — not applicable to stucco wall field. All tiers require primer (alkali-resistant on traditional stucco is not quality-optional).

configuration_dimensions.description: Stucco substrate type. Primary branching dimension driving coating system constraint, primer selection, pressure wash settings, LRV constraints, and insurance requirements.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Traditional stucco: Portland cement/sand/lime, pH up to 13, requires alkali-resistant primer. EIFS: EPS + polymer base + acrylic finish, no alkalinity concern, requires 100% acrylic coatings. HARD CONSTRAINT: EIFS = acrylic coating ONLY — elastomeric PROHIBITED. Per-elevation if mixed substrate types on same structure.

configuration_dimensions.description: Stucco texture profile. Drives DUAL multiplier on both labor rate (SF/hr) and material consumption (SF/gal). Dominant cost driver for stucco estimation.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Smooth=1.00x baseline. Sand=1.25x (both labor and material). Lace (Spanish lace)=1.50x. Dash/roughcast=2.00x. Also drives roller nap selection: smooth 3/4-1 inch, sand 1-1/4 inch, lace/dash 1-1/4 to 1-1/2 inch. Per-elevation if texture varies.

configuration_dimensions.description: Coating system for finish coats. Acrylic is standard; elastomeric is for crack-bridging on traditional stucco only.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Acrylic: 10-20 perms breathability, 4-6 mils DFT, 300-350 SF/gal smooth. Elastomeric: 5-15 perms, 12-20 mils DFT, >300% elongation, 100-175 SF/gal smooth. HARD CONSTRAINT: EIFS = acrylic ONLY — elastomeric PROHIBITED (catastrophic moisture entrapment). Elastomeric not available at QT2. Elastomeric is flat-only sheen. Material cost 5-8x higher than acrylic per SF.

configuration_dimensions.description: Primary application technique for prime and finish coats.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Spray_backroll is gold standard for stucco — spray auto-adds backroll (MANDATORY per Exterior Application Methods Doctrine Part A section 6). Spray-only is PROHIBITED on textured stucco (backroll forces coating into texture recesses). Roll is fallback for smaller areas or occupied-adjacent. Brush is detail work only. Spray_backroll requires 2-person crew.

Flat is most common for stucco wall field (hides texture irregularities). Satin for EIFS (easier cleaning). Semi-gloss not typical for stucco — magnifies texture irregularities. Elastomeric coating system is flat-only.

paintable_items.name: Exterior Stucco Wall Field Surface
paintable_items.counting_rules: Net paintable stucco/EIFS wall field area in square feet. Excludes window/door openings, trim elements. Measured per elevation from PaintScope.
paintable_items.notes: Single paintable item. Covers both traditional 3-coat stucco and EIFS/synthetic stucco wall surfaces. Substrate_type dimension drives primer selection and coating system constraint. Texture_profile dimension drives dual labor+material multiplier.

valid_input_states.notes: SS_EXT_BARE_MASONRY is the single NC state for both traditional stucco and EIFS. All new stucco arrives bare/uncoated. Traditional stucco is cementitious (same chemical family as masonry). Repaint states would require a separate spec.

output_state.notes: Output state varies by sheen configuration. Flat is the most common exterior stucco sheen.

traditional_stucco.notes: Alkali-resistant primer MANDATORY on ALL new traditional stucco (pH 12-14). Standard acrylic primer is NOT suitable.

EIFS.notes: Standard 100% acrylic exterior primer for EIFS. No alkalinity concern. Vapor-permeable formulation preferred.

material_systems.name: Alkali-Resistant Primer for Traditional Stucco
material_systems.notes: MANDATORY on ALL new traditional stucco regardless of quality tier. pH 12-14 requires alkali-resistant primer (e.g., SW Loxon Masonry Primer rated to pH 13). Standard acrylic primer NOT suitable. Enables 7-day accelerated coating vs 28-day standard cure. Coverage is texture-dependent — smooth 300-350 SF/gal, sand 225-275, lace 150-200, dash 75-125.

material_systems.name: 100% Acrylic Exterior Primer for EIFS
material_systems.notes: Standard 100% acrylic exterior primer for EIFS. No alkalinity concern — standard acrylic is suitable. Vapor-permeable formulation preferred. 350-450 SF/gal (smoother, less porous than traditional stucco).

material_systems.name: Standard 100% Acrylic Exterior Finish for Stucco
material_systems.notes: 100% acrylic exterior latex. 10-20 perms breathability. 4-6 mils DFT. QT2 single coat, QT3 two coats. Valid for both traditional stucco and EIFS. Coverage is texture-dependent — smooth 300-350 SF/gal, sand 200-275, lace 150-200, dash 75-125, EIFS 350-400.

material_systems.name: Premium 100% Acrylic Exterior Finish for Stucco
material_systems.notes: Premium 100% acrylic (SW Duration, BM Aura Exterior). 10-20 perms. Raking light inspection between coats. Two coats standard. Valid for both traditional stucco and EIFS.

material_systems.name: Elastomeric Coating for Traditional Stucco
material_systems.notes: Elastomeric: 12-20 mils DFT, >300% elongation, bridges hairline cracks. Two coats mandatory. STRICTLY PROHIBITED on EIFS (catastrophic moisture entrapment). Not available at QT2. Material cost 5-8x higher per SF than acrylic. Requires moisture source assessment.

Alkali primer spray_backroll/roll (traditional), acrylic primer spray_backroll/roll (EIFS), brush detail
Acrylic spray_backroll/roll, elastomeric spray_backroll/roll, brush detail — first coat
Intercoat inspection, sand (QT4 only on anomalies), dust removal
Second finish coat — same task structure as coat 1
Protection teardown, equipment cleaning, waste disposal

factor_modifiers.description: DUAL production rate AND material consumption modifier by stucco texture profile
Production rate modifier by stucco substrate type (labor only)
Quality tier modifier for binary tasks

production_summary.worst_case_scenario: Dash texture (2.00) x traditional stucco (1.00) x scaffold (1.60) x QT4 (1.20) = 3.84x on elastomeric spray_backroll — 90 SF/hr base becomes 23 SF/hr effective

compatibility_rules.description: Oil-based and alkyd products PROHIBITED on all stucco substrates
compatibility_rules.notes: Traditional stucco: alkaline hydroxides cause saponification. EIFS: oil-based products dissolve EPS insulation board. Water-based acrylic or elastomeric only.

compatibility_rules.description: Elastomeric coatings PROHIBITED on EIFS — HARD BLOCKER
compatibility_rules.notes: Single most critical material routing rule. Elastomeric on EIFS traps moisture behind EPS board — mold growth, substrate deterioration, catastrophic delamination. No exceptions.
Low LRV (dark colors) absorb excessive solar heat, causing EPS expansion/contraction and potential delamination. Dark colors void most EIFS manufacturer warranties.

compatibility_rules.description: Traditional stucco MUST use alkali-resistant primer
compatibility_rules.notes: New traditional stucco pH up to 13 requires alkali-resistant primer. Standard acrylic primer will suffer alkali burn. Non-negotiable at all quality tiers.
Elastomeric application complexity (thick-film DFT control, heavy-body spray, mandatory 2-coat system) exceeds economy scope.

compatibility_rules.description: Spray on stucco requires backroll — no spray-only
compatibility_rules.notes: Stucco texture creates voids and shadowed areas. Back-rolling forces coating into texture recesses. Per Application Methods Doctrine Part A section 6.

compatibility_rules.description: Elastomeric coating requires moisture source assessment
compatibility_rules.notes: Elastomeric has reduced vapor permeability. Moisture from alternate sources becomes trapped, causing catastrophic delamination.

compatibility_rules.description: Cracks >1/8 inch are HARD STOP — structural assessment required
compatibility_rules.notes: Cosmetic cracks <1/8 inch can be patched. Cracks >1/8 inch indicate structural movement. Applies to both substrate types. Do not coat over structural cracks.

round_configurations.name: Prime + 2 Finish Coats (QT3/QT4, Acrylic, Both Substrate Types)
round_configurations.notes: Standard stucco sequence. Primer (alkali-resistant for traditional, acrylic for EIFS) + 2 acrylic finish coats.

round_configurations.name: Prime + 1 Finish Coat (QT2, Both Substrate Types)
round_configurations.notes: Economy stucco. Single acrylic finish coat on primed surface. Elastomeric not available at QT2.

round_configurations.name: Prime + 2 Elastomeric Finish Coats (Traditional Stucco QT3/QT4)
round_configurations.notes: Elastomeric sequence. Higher DFT per coat. Target cumulative 12-20 mils. Traditional stucco ONLY.

variants.notes: Economy spray_backroll on smooth traditional stucco. Alkali-resistant primer + single acrylic finish coat.
Standard spray_backroll acrylic on smooth traditional stucco. Baseline scenario — 137 SF/hr finish rate.
Elastomeric on sand traditional stucco. Dual multiplier: 1.25x labor + 1.25x material. Flat sheen only.
EIFS acrylic. Fastest variant — EIFS substrate modifier 0.90x (10% faster). LRV >20 color constraint.
Premium acrylic on lace traditional stucco. Texture 1.50x + QT4 1.20x stacking.
Worst-case scenario: dash texture (2.00x) + elastomeric + QT4. Maximum modifier stacking 3.84x on scaffold. 23 SF/hr effective rate. Flat sheen only.
Standard roll-only acrylic on sand traditional stucco. Reduced protection — no patio cover (no overspray). 1-person crew.
Roll-only EIFS acrylic. No overspray. 1-person crew. Reduced protection scope.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Window casing or stucco pop-out trim at openings. Stucco terminates at opening. Separate spec.
Door casing trim. Same as window casing relationship. Separate spec.
Soffit underside at eave junction. Often different color. Separate scope.
Foundation below stucco wall. Not painted in this scope.
Frieze or band board at stucco-to-soffit junction (if present). Trim scope.

cross_spec_boundaries.notes: Window/door protection during stucco wall work is NOT this spec's responsibility. Prevents double-counting.
Corner boards, frieze, rake, window/door casing — all separate from stucco wall field.
Soffit underside at stucco-to-eave junction — separate scope.
Below-grade and earth-contact surfaces require different coating systems and prep.
Wind, dew point, surface temperature are scheduling/process concerns per RC-003 pattern. Not estimatable at bid time.

site_condition_rules.affected_tasks: All tasks performed at elevation (see FAC_EXT_ACCESS applies_to list in production.json)
site_condition_rules.effect: ground=1.00, ladder=1.35, scaffold=1.60, lift=1.50. Applied as time multiplier: effective_rate = base_rate / modifier.
site_condition_rules.notes: Access type is a height modifier, NOT a site condition. Applied per elevation. Scaffold is common for multi-story stucco (long continuous runs at height).

risk_flags.description: CGL insurance policies commonly exclude EIFS work. Contractor may be uninsured without explicit policy coverage or EIFS-specific rider. Mandatory photo documentation of pre-existing conditions.
risk_flags.mitigation: Verify CGL coverage includes EIFS before accepting projects. Obtain EIFS-specific rider if needed.

risk_flags.topic: Elastomeric on EIFS — catastrophic moisture entrapment
risk_flags.description: Elastomeric coatings applied to EIFS trap moisture behind EPS board, causing mold growth, substrate deterioration, and catastrophic system delamination.
risk_flags.mitigation: NEVER apply elastomeric on EIFS. HARD BLOCKER — no exceptions. EIFS = 100% acrylic only.

risk_flags.topic: Elastomeric moisture risk on traditional stucco
risk_flags.description: Elastomeric has reduced vapor permeability. If moisture enters from alternate sources (ground water, plumbing leaks, rising damp), it becomes trapped behind the elastomeric film, causing catastrophic delamination.
risk_flags.mitigation: Moisture source assessment required before specifying elastomeric. Verify no alternate moisture sources.

risk_flags.description: Cracks >1/8 inch indicate structural movement requiring engineering evaluation. Cannot be patched — painting scope hard stop.
risk_flags.mitigation: Crack assessment is FIRST prep task. >1/8 inch = STOP work, refer to structural engineer.

risk_flags.topic: EIFS dark color thermal stress (LRV constraint)
risk_flags.description: Dark colors (LRV <20) on EIFS absorb excessive solar heat, causing EPS thermal cycling, delamination, and finish coat cracking. Voids most EIFS warranties.
risk_flags.mitigation: Verify color LRV >20 (preferably >50) for all EIFS work. Document LRV verification.

risk_flags.topic: Elastomeric material cost escalation on textured stucco
risk_flags.description: Dash texture + elastomeric = extreme material consumption. A 2000 SF dash wall may consume 60-70 gallons of elastomeric (2 coats) at $50-80/gal. Material cost alone $3,500-5,600 vs $560-900 for acrylic.
risk_flags.mitigation: Flag material cost escalation at specification time. Ensure elastomeric is justified by crack-bridging need.

sequencing_notes.production_sequence: Setup -> Prep -> Prime -> Finish 1 -> Interstage (QT3/QT4) -> Finish 2 (QT3/QT4) -> Final Inspect -> Cleanup
sequencing_notes.edge_work: No edge work in this spec. Stucco terminates at openings and trim elements — no cut-in or blending across specs.
sequencing_notes.protection_sequence: Landscape/hardscape protection -> Fixture/HVAC masking -> Equipment setup -> Coating work -> Protection teardown -> Equipment cleanup -> Site cleanup
sequencing_notes.coat_sequence: Crack assess (FIRST) -> EIFS knock test (EIFS) -> Moisture test (traditional) -> Cure verify (traditional) -> EIFS insurance verify (EIFS) -> Pressure wash (branched by substrate) -> Dry time -> Mildew treat (conditional) -> Efflorescence treat (traditional, conditional) -> Crack patch (conditional) -> Surface patch -> Caulk joints -> Prime -> Finish 1 -> Interstage (QT3/QT4) -> Finish 2 (QT3/QT4) -> Final inspect -> Touch up
sequencing_notes.elevation_strategy: Work one elevation at a time to minimize protection setup/teardown cycles. Follow shade for optimal conditions. Scaffold moves per elevation.
sequencing_notes.key_prohibitions: NO spray-only on stucco (backroll mandatory). NO oil-based or alkyd products. NO elastomeric on EIFS. NO coating at MC > 12% (traditional). NO elastomeric at QT2. NO high-pressure wash on EIFS (>500 PSI damages system). NO coating over structural cracks (>1/8 inch).

relationships.cross_spec_protection_note: Window/door protection during stucco work is owned by window/door specs, not this spec.
relationships.notes: Shares cementitious substrate family with masonry sibling. Key departures from masonry: no block filler module (stucco has continuous surface), texture_profile dual multiplier (masonry uses substrate_type modifier), EIFS substrate with acrylic-only hard constraint, separate pressure wash tasks by substrate type. Shares protection zone pattern with all exterior siblings.

sections_used: Spray_backroll mandatory on stucco Part A §6

change_log.author: SpecFactory
change_log.changes: Initial draft spec for exterior stucco/EIFS wall coating. Key features: combined prime+paint (single mobilization), 2 substrate types (traditional_stucco/EIFS) with HARD CONSTRAINT (EIFS = acrylic only), 4 texture profiles (smooth/sand/lace/dash) with DUAL labor+material multiplier, 2 coating systems (acrylic/elastomeric), 3 application methods (spray_backroll/roll/brush — spray-only prohibited), 2 sheens (flat/satin), 3 quality tiers (QT2-QT4, QT5 excluded), 41 tasks across 8 modules, 5 material systems (2 primers + 3 finish), 4 factor modifiers (texture/substrate_type/access/QT), 3 round configurations, 8 compatibility rules. Max modifier stacking 3.84x under 4.0x cap. No block filler module (unlike masonry). Stucco tape required for masking on textured surfaces. EIFS insurance verification workflow gate.
